note_sections.t: Clinical review prompted by a previously negative biopsy and steadily increasing prostate-specific antigen measurements.

A 59-year-old warehouse manager entered initial evaluation for an incidental PSA elevation in late 2023. Serum levels have climbed from 22.0 ng/mL to 35.0 ng/mL over the preceding twelve months, despite the earlier negative biopsy result. He is an ex-smoker (27 pack-yr, quit 2008). Alcohol consumption averages 28 units weekly. Physical activity remains largely sedentary, punctuated by occasional walks. He is married and lives in assisted-living facility, where his spouse serves as the primary contact. Hearing impairment is present, and he consistently prefers written clinical summaries. Recent non-urological appointments include a pain clinic visit for chronic shoulder discomfort, routine dental check-ups, and six physiotherapy sessions for lower back stiffness. He denies hematuria, bone pain, or unexplained weight loss. Comorbidities are none. Active medication is none. Normal DRE.

DRE — texture: firm and symmetrically enlarged; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: absent. General examination remains unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no palpable lymphadenopathy or bone tenderness.
